items.item_text: BA or equivalent degree and experience.
Experience in financial analysis with large volumes of complex data. Experience conducting research and preparing break-even analyses, variance analyses, and feasibility studies.
Experience with statistical data collection techniques and quantitative analysis.
Experience advising managers on complex financial and budget analysis tasks.
Experience making presentations to groups, facilitating group discussions, and achieving consensus from disparate perspectives.
Experience using initiative, problem diagnosis, and proactive problem solving skills to develop and apply creative innovative concepts to problem resolution.

Experience with fund accounting and general accounting principles and techniques to apply to budgeting, rate development, and financial reporting. Experience monitoring and managing a complex budget using an automated accounting system.

Experience using Microsoft Office products (Excel, Word, and PowerPoint) or other automation tools to perform complex spreadsheet analyses, formulate and prepare complex reports, and prepare sophisticated presentations.

Under general guidance of the UC Center Sacramento Director and Associate Director, perform budgetary and financial functions for UC Center Sacramento and represent UC Center Sacramento in meetings and discussions as needed at both the campus (UC Davis) level and at UC system-wide meetings. Ensure appropriate accounting and internal controls are maintained. Prepare and establish budgets, organize resources according to budgetary plans, prepare both routine and ad hoc financial reports using data from the general ledger and departmental or project budgets, and forecast revenue and expenses. Assist in the development of unit budget, fees, rates for recharge service, and other income sources. Coordinate the development and management of Service Level Agreements (SLAs) and Memorandum of Understandings (MOUs).

Interpersonal and communication skills to interact and communicate professionally and collaboratively with management and staff, using diplomacy during all interactions in the performance of a wide variety of programs and support functions.
Knowledge of public sector business practices, entrepreneurial operations, and fund management. Familiarity with issues related to state government and policy.
Knowledge of University of California and University of California, Davis, policies and procedures pertaining to financial administration, payroll, personnel, and other business-related activities.
